title: Royal Spanish Academy
exportLabel: Molen original Royal Spanish Academy headquarters shared-surface source
visualBrief: Complete principal Madrid headquarters exterior: red-brick rectangular main block with pale basement and attic, all four windowed elevations, eleven-bay north frontage with closed secondary door and small balcony, east principal four-column fluted Doric portico with genuinely open intercolumniation, closed entablature and triangular pediment, three closed entry doors and integral descending stairs, low closed slate hip roof with eight brick chimneys, continuous belt courses, dentil cornice and original geometric attic reliefs and pediment figures. Independent garden fence/gates, transient flags, vegetation, street furniture and neighbors remain native. No navigable interior or exact inscription/sculptural likeness is claimed.

references.observed: Actually inspected the complete north/east oblique: red brick main body over pale basement, pale attic band with alternating tall glazed windows and original geometric relief panels, heavy dentil cornice, dark low roof with brick chimneys. East principal portico has four tall pale fluted Doric columns, genuine open intercolumniation, a deep entablature and closed triangular pediment with simplified corner/peak figures. Broad entrance stairs and closed timber doors are partly obscured by railings/trees. North side has two rows of framed windows, a central secondary door and small balcony. No roof courtyard appears in map; rear details are inferred.

Actually inspected the full north frontage: eleven bays on both brick stories, central closed secondary door with small stone balcony above, alternating triangular and horizontal upper window heads, continuous pale belt/base courses, tall narrow attic windows alternating square relief panels, dentil cornice and several brick chimneys. Ground and basement follow a slight street slope. Exact sculptural/lettered detail is omitted in favor of original geometric interpretation.

Catalog Q11993457 identifies the institution, not a unique building. The modeled principal Madrid headquarters is the named Real Academia Española map building and same-ID POI 35184457607397 at Felipe IV,4, checked against two ordinary north/east pictures.
